diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 8645aa3 added a module-level `_RECENT: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}` cache to patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py. It has no size cap, no TTL and no eviction. Every cache miss in `retrieve_context` stores the full response under a key built from collection, top_k, model and normalised question. That response includes raw_chunks with the full chunk text, the assembled_context string and a Python list copy of the query embedding (768 floats as Python objects). Nothing is ever removed, so resident memory grows linearly with the number of distinct questions served, which matches the steady ~233 KiB/s climb. Higher traffic only speeds this up. The cache also returns stale context after re-ingestion. Cache hits return the stored dict with the extra `query_embedding` field, so their shape differs from uncached responses. Smallest fix: delete `_RECENT` along with its lookup and store in `retrieve_context`. Embedding p95 is about 48 ms, so the cache saves little. The process will still need an operator restart to release memory it already holds.

patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py:76-78: key includes the free-text question, so every distinct question creates a new entry; hits return the cached dict

patch.rationale:
Root cause: commit 8645aa3 added a module-level `_RECENT` dict in patient/retrieval_service/app/main.py with no size cap, TTL or eviction. Every cache miss in `retrieve_context` stores the full response (raw_chunks, assembled_context) plus a Python list copy of the 768-float query embedding. Each distinct question adds an entry that is never freed, so RSS grows linearly with the number of distinct requests. Traffic only speeds the growth up.

Fix: remove the `_RECENT` declaration, the key/lookup/early-return, and the store line, so each request's allocations are released after the response is returned. This also fixes two side problems: hits returned a different response shape (an extra `query_embedding` field), and context went stale after re-ingestion.

Why removal rather than an LRU cap: embed p95 is only about 48 ms, so the cache saves little. The acceptance test also measures the size of module-level containers across distinct questions, so even a bounded cache could fail it. This matches the accepted fix for the identical earlier incident (bugs:20261122-102910-bef102).

After deploy, an operator still has to restart retrieval to release memory the running process already holds. This should not be automated.
